name: Remitting seronegative symmetrical synovitis with pitting oedema (RS3PE)
aliases: remitting seronegative symmetrical synovitis with pitting edema

clinicalPearls: Characterised by abrupt-onset, symmetrical polysynovitis with striking pitting oedema of the dorsum of the hands and feet
Predominantly affects elderly patients, more often men, and is seronegative for rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibodies
The oedema reflects tenosynovitis of the extensor and flexor tendon sheaths rather than joint effusion alone
Typically shows a dramatic and rapid response to low-dose corticosteroids, which is a useful diagnostic and therapeutic feature
Overlaps clinically with polymyalgia rheumatica and elderly-onset seronegative rheumatoid arthritis
Carries a recognised paraneoplastic association, so occult solid organ and haematological malignancy should be considered, particularly with atypical or steroid-resistant disease
Generally follows a remitting course with a good outcome once malignancy has been excluded
reference.pathophysiology: RS3PE is a seronegative inflammatory arthropathy of older adults in which acute symmetrical synovitis and tenosynovitis produce distal pitting oedema of the hands and feet. Increased vascular permeability, linked to raised levels of vascular endothelial growth factor and pro-inflammatory cytokines, is thought to underlie the prominent subcutaneous oedema surrounding the inflamed tendon sheaths. The condition may be idiopathic or arise as a paraneoplastic phenomenon accompanying solid organ or haematological malignancy, and it shares immunopathogenic features with polymyalgia rheumatica and other seronegative arthropathies of the elderly.
additionalInvestigations: Inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP), which are typically markedly raised
Rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibodies, which are characteristically negative
Ultrasound or MRI of the hands demonstrating tenosynovitis and soft-tissue oedema
Age-appropriate malignancy screening given the paraneoplastic association
Full blood count and blood film to screen for haematological disease
redFlags: Constitutional symptoms (weight loss, night sweats) suggesting underlying malignancy
Poor or absent response to corticosteroids, prompting a search for occult cancer
Relapse after steroid withdrawal raising concern for an evolving malignancy or alternative diagnosis
New lymphadenopathy or organomegaly on examination
reference.prognosis: Idiopathic RS3PE usually remits within months and responds excellently to low-dose corticosteroids with a favourable long-term outlook; however, paraneoplastic cases carry the prognosis of the underlying malignancy, making cancer surveillance essential.
pitfalls: Failing to screen for occult malignancy, especially with atypical or steroid-resistant presentations
Mislabelling as seronegative rheumatoid arthritis and committing to long-term DMARD therapy unnecessarily
Attributing the distal oedema to heart failure or venous disease and missing the synovitis
Stopping corticosteroids too abruptly and misinterpreting relapse
management: Low-dose oral corticosteroids as first-line therapy, typically producing a rapid and dramatic response
Gradual corticosteroid taper over months, guided by resolution of symptoms and inflammatory markers
NSAIDs as adjunctive symptomatic relief where appropriate
Age-appropriate malignancy screening given the paraneoplastic association, especially in atypical or steroid-resistant disease
Monitoring for relapse and for evolution into polymyalgia rheumatica or elderly-onset seronegative rheumatoid arthritis
Rheumatology referral for diagnostic confirmation and guidance on corticosteroid management
